implementation.notes: ProjectStore saves immutable snapshots through validated staging and publication. Project-store fixtures cover exact-revision snapshot saves, post-snapshot edits that do not leak into saved bytes, compare-and-swap destination checks, verified backups, external-change rejection, injected pre-publication rollback, and staging-handle/path tamper resistance. Clean-machine storage-fault evidence and the production gate remain open. Current Debug/Release acceptance evidence is hash-bound to the named sources and fixtures; the qualification boundary remains explicit. Compact mixed-asset proof 9 removes duplicate binary/metadata payloads from measured-wall completion JSON while preserving full immutable assets, strict resolver identity checks and exact deterministic replay. Native26/extraction24 apply across retained Undo/deleted history and recovery; legacy inline7/corner8 remain distinct. Rigid selected-wall proof4/envelope10 uses native27/extraction25 and can retain the same compact supplemental references without borrowing exterior authority. Focused core/native/extraction checks cover 530 KiB and 10 MiB assets, metadata-only edits, erases/no-ops, exact numeric forms and recomputed-digest tamper/downgrade refusal. Existing resource limits and broader production qualifications remain unchanged.

implementation.notes: Analytical line and circular-arc geometry, closure, winding, intersections, tangency, and boundary validation are implemented. Shared line/arc contacts use a local chord-frame solve rather than subtracting large radius squares; canvas directional alignment uses that same kernel. Room-hole topology validates each hole plus strict containment, disjoint interiors, and no contact or nesting analytically, rejecting indeterminate cases closed. Separate shallow-arc containment and arc/arc numerical qualification, independent high-precision fixture parity, broader topology workflows, and the production gate remain open. Historical Debug/Release evidence retains its named-source qualification boundary; this requirement remains in progress.

requirements.delivery_notes: October 9 source-only corrections preserve actual near-tangent arc/arc roots and prevent rounded origin translation from proving an exact tangent. An endpoint-anchored circle certificate admits shared-endpoint tangencies across sweeps and rotations only when the entire second-root distance/error band fits within tolerance. A bounded rational fallback now retries indeterminate contacts on original binary64 inputs, certifying strict gaps, genuine roots and rotated nonshared interior half-turn tangency. Complete root/output enclosures guard merging and all endpoint classifications. Analytical arc/arc minimum-distance candidates and certified contact absence preserve strict topology clearance for new internal misses and hole boundaries. Selected-arc projection bounds now independently prove strict separation in x/y, diagonal and original-chord-normal directions, including opposed nearly concentric subarcs and long separated pieces missed by fixed directions; unresolved radical axes and discriminants can use that gap without fabricating a contact. The projected gap must exceed twice tolerance to exclude supporting-circle roots tolerated near both endpoints as well as actual contact and tolerance-close geometry. Projections retain uncertain membership and share fixed arithmetic budgets. Generic trigonometric zero and uncertain clearance cases without an independent gap proof still reject conservatively. Numerical and runtime qualification remain required. See docs/delivery/progress.md and docs/geometry-operations.md. No changed-source compilation or runtime acceptance is claimed.

implementation.notes: The constraint editor supports persisted endpoint relationships for straight and analytical curved walls and identified measurement/room boundaries, including mixed components. Physical curve length is a separate version-3 relation at fixed signed sweep; anchored target editing changes actual geometry while endpoint distance retains chord semantics. Retained physical-length relations require project format 12 and exchange version 9. Direct curved-wall resize now uses physical arc length without adding a lock, preserving the chosen endpoint and signed sweep. It records proof 3 in command 5 and a physical input receipt 2, requiring project format 13 and exchange 10 even when the receipt was imported without history. Native previews show actual arcs, exact input survives persistence, and persistent coordinate freedom remains separate from temporary anchors. Version-2 curved endpoint proofs retain their previous semantics. Fresh and archived measured curves now preserve exact original construction through shared rigid-transform replay for rotation, reflection, translation and cloning. Archive version 2 requires project format 14 and exchange 11 across imported, undone and deleted history. Explicit reconstruction invalidates a stale known length receipt and refuses opaque metadata loss. Measured-wall scaling, tangency, level dependency propagation and full production qualification remain open. Historical acceptance artifacts do not certify this checkpoint. Receipt-backed measured strokes now support all six endpoint relations plus fixed anchor and physical arc length, including terminal/revisited vertices and mixed wall/boundary components. requirements.title: Support selection and clipboard operations for geometry, areas, annotations, and architectural objects.
requirements.remaining_behavior: Copy, cut, paste, multi-select, and selection filtering preserve semantic links and produce undoable commands.
required_variants: Copy, cut, paste, multi-select, and selection filtering preserve semantic links and produce undoable commands.
requirements.expected_result: Copy, cut, paste, multi-select, and selection filtering preserve semantic links and produce undoable commands.
assertions: Copy, cut, paste, multi-select, and selection filtering preserve semantic links and produce undoable commands.

implementation.notes: Bounded local JSON clipboard supports copy, paste, cut, and guarded delete for supported geometry graphs. Ctrl-click toggles ordered selection roots, both plan canvases highlight the selection, and combined clipboard/delete commands deduplicate hosted dependencies in one revision and undo/redo step; paste preserves root order with fresh identities and remapped links. Canvas movement combines compatible architectural objects, individual annotation instances, and reference images in one admitted command, retaining owner metadata and wall measurements; partial constrained-group moves reject without publishing any member. Source or selection replacement cancels captured mouse gestures. Native movement evidence covers history, save/reopen, conflicts, and stale release; the development-host reference fixture tests downstream editing after asserting isolated import rejection, not decoder acceptance. Paste selects mapped annotation children rather than invisible owner containers, exposing immediate canvas transforms. Transforms resolve unique owners and preserve admitted raw metadata; older annotation states upgrade completely for independent axis resizing. Copy now slices selected labels/symbols, merges same-owner subsets, preserves raw artwork/transform/text/opaque metadata and carries only their targeted overrides. Individual and mixed annotation cut/delete update owners atomically while preserving unselected siblings; explicit whole-owner selection dominates child selection. Cut publishes its prepared clipboard only after document commit. Native clipboard coverage includes multiple owners, hosted geometry, fresh identities, history, save/reopen, invalid and read-only refusal. Both plan canvases now offer category filtering for new click, Ctrl-click, window/crossing marquee, double-click and context picks. Filtering retains scene content and existing transforms; excluded occupied content cannot start idle drawing. Independent nested ANSI appraisal copies retain complete dependency graphs and source-specific appearance/dimensions; source ownership stays unchanged, and copied sloped evidence remains unqualified until observed confirmation. Supported destination policy, site scope, stair bindings, stale deep sources and cyclic graphs have explicit admission rules. See docs/verification/nested-appraisal-copy-2026-10-04.md for the scoped runtime evidence. Broader linked-object policies and production qualification remain open. Current historical Debug/Release acceptance evidence remains hash-bound to its named sources and fixtures; this scoped checkpoint does not certify full parity. Saved measured-stroke length/angle dimensions now follow replay-backed geometry, source-owned rigid placements, mixed canvas movement, independent clone/clipboard, editable reopen and shared SVG/PDF projection. Native36/extraction34 protect retained bindings. This focused evidence does not recertify historical acceptance or establish Apex native compatibility, full output parity or ANSI approval.

implementation.notes: Segment-length dimensions have stable references and an inspector for position, paper text height, color, bold/italic, rotation, and visibility. Version 2 presentation survives save/reopen, undo/redo, and boundary transforms. Shared canvas/sheet rendering preserves paper text size across model output scales and fitted previews, with pixel/DPI and rotated-hit tests. Straight segment dimensions now regenerate matching extension and dimension linework from the stable source edge in both canvases and shared output; curved segment dimensions use a true offset analytical arc with radial extension lines. Semantic angle dimensions reference two stable segments plus their shared vertex and derive current tangent angles; area dimensions reference a complete closed boundary and derive current area. Both kinds persist, recalculate after geometry edits, render through the shared canvas/output path, and can be created from the offline dimension dialog through normal undoable commands. Apex workflow parity, compatibility certification, and complete output qualification remain open. Deterministic Debug/Release workflow evidence is hash-bound to the named sources and fixtures; the qualification boundary remains explicit. Saved measured-stroke length/angle dimensions now follow replay-backed geometry, source-owned rigid placements, mixed canvas movement, independent clone/clipboard, editable reopen and shared SVG/PDF projection. Native36/extraction34 protect retained bindings. This focused evidence does not recertify historical acceptance or establish Apex native compatibility, full output parity or ANSI approval. Saved callout canvas dragging uses shared presentation preparation and exact preview admission, preserving measured geometry and values. Complete physical perimeter/callout groups use source-aware rigid movement, without silently expanding into unselected geometry. Partial physical-wall/callout groups now compose connected solver geometry with narrow typed original-position placement in one reversible command; ordinary labels can accompany walls without an exterior owner. Explicit coincidence classes preserve exact joins without weakening topology or moving fixed anchors. Native41/extraction39 retain envelope15 across history and transfer. Mixed complete-plus-partial perimeters and broader multi-object compositions remain in scope; focused native evidence does not close full acceptance. See partial-wall-callout-movement-2026-10-04.md. See dimension-callout-drag-2026-10-04.md for scoped verification.

assertions: Style and fill changes affect presentation only, persist across save/reopen, and do not alter analytical geometry.

implementation.notes: Presentation styles, fills, visibility, and target overrides are validated separately from analytical geometry. The shared desktop appearance editor changes closed-area or physical building-object outline/fill colors, fill pattern, hatch scale, paper line width and visibility, or resets only that target. Revision-guarded raw edits preserve owner protection, opaque metadata and siblings. Object styles apply after physical plan/elevation/section projection, including multiple shapes belonging to one source, and remain independent of measurement labels. Quick properties and contextual actions expose the physical-object editor; hidden objects remain recoverable through Layers. Focused native workflows exercise rendered output, history, save/reopen, no-op, reset, stale/read-only and source preservation. Saved plan/elevation/section views now retain independent whole-view and physical-object style/visibility, resolved once for canvas and sheet/PDF. Graph-owner and local-view identity prevent cross-view edits and labels. Hosted openings inherit resolved host visibility; hidden presentation overlays do not block visible output. Native fixtures cover actual editor controls, source preservation, same-sheet independent colors, full scene hiding/recovery, exact owner identity, history, native reopen, deletion repair and legacy/current clipboard remapping. Optional model7 appearance requires native24/extraction22 across all retained history, with downgrade refusal and strict reference admission. SVG components now retain optional per-instance outline/surface colors using an immutable derived render copy and palette-aware cache. Quick properties expose Colors and library reset; source bytes, gradients, protected recess/glass paint, geometry, owner policy and opaque metadata survive targeted edits, clipboard, history and native reopen. Annotation7/native25/extraction23 preserve explicit intent across all retained history. Native fixtures cover independent same-artwork colors on screen and actual PDF, reset/no-op/cancel/stale/read-only behavior, unsupported saved profile diagnostics and refusal preserving an existing PDF and fingerprint sidecar, then recovery through reset. All 322 catalog assets pass the explicit paint-role contract. Exact saved-view previews now resolve immutable uncropped sources through the same visibility/style policy as the committed canvas, including locally recovered walls and hosted openings entering a crop. Native checks cover graph-owner identity, source/host/child masks, numeric Preview/Cancel/Apply/Undo and preview/commit agreement. Full production visual/print qualification remains open; this scoped implementation does not certify full parity or shaded 3D material editing. Historical evidence remains hash-bound to its original sources and fixtures.

implementation.notes: Local save/open and bounded native DXF/IFC mapping are implemented. The DXF desktop review assigns source layers to existing destinations across floors or creates source-named layers on the active floor, preserves exact source bytes and commits one undoable import. Planar CIRCLE records now reconstruct exact two-semicircle boundaries, including uniform signed/rotated INSERTs and source-unit conversion. Nonuniform or numerically unrepresentable circles require retained-source diagnostics. Expanded primitive work is preflighted before candidate creation. Native block activation compares circle content as well as the existing generated plan primitives. Label/symbol export now uses each child's assigned native layer with explicit broken-reference diagnostics. These scoped implementations do not certify native Apex import/export, legacy exchange or external consumer fidelity. Native36/extraction34 protect retained bindings. This focused evidence does not recertify historical acceptance or establish Apex native compatibility, full output parity or ANSI approval.

requirements.title: Support mouse, keyboard, active pen, and touch input for precision drawing and editing.
requirements.remaining_behavior: Recorded mouse/keyboard, real pen, and real touch fixtures complete core draw/edit operations with correct focus, pressure-independent geometry, and undo.
required_variants: Recorded mouse/keyboard, real pen, and real touch fixtures complete core draw/edit operations with correct focus, pressure-independent geometry, and undo.
requirements.expected_result: Recorded mouse/keyboard, real pen, and real touch fixtures complete core draw/edit operations with correct focus, pressure-independent geometry, and undo.
assertions: Recorded mouse/keyboard, real pen, and real touch fixtures complete core draw/edit operations with correct focus, pressure-independent geometry, and undo.

implementation.notes: Mouse and keyboard drawing/editing remain on the shared canvas command path. Plan canvases explicitly accept Qt touch and tablet events and route them through the same focus, snapping, selection, navigation, and undo-capable commands; stylus pressure is not used as geometry input. Two-finger touch navigation cancels pending one-finger edits, pans and zooms around a moving model anchor, rebases changed contact pairs, and prevents finger-lift handoff from authoring geometry. Cancellation, focus loss, hide and modal transitions discard touch ownership. Qt-delivered regression events cover pinch, pan, contact changes, edit cancellation, zoom limits and output invariance. Real pen/touch hardware runs, gesture ergonomics, and complete production acceptance remain open.

requirements.remaining_behavior: Opening fixtures host, move, resize, replace, schedule, and export without losing wall geometry or handedness data.

implementation.notes: Hosted door/window cuts now use a single dimension editor with live unrolled elevation preview, complete host-opening semantic validation, revision/context fencing, and one-command undo/redo. Optional versioned handing and swing now drive creation, inspector edits, analytic plan leaf/arc geometry, and schedule cells, with save/reopen and geometry tests. Newly authored openings receive a strict version-1 opening_assembly profile; the shared OCCT kernel derives frame, leaf/sash, and glazing solids under the stable opening ID while preserving the authoritative wall cut, dimensions, and handedness. Legacy openings remain valid without the optional profile. The opening inspector now edits frame width/depth, panel or sash depth, glazing depth, and signed inset through one revision-checked command with preview and undo/redo coverage. Scaling a host wall scales its authoritative opening and assembly dimensions atomically, including negative inset, with OCCT volume, preview, undo/redo, and save/reopen checks. Straight-host doors, windows and bare openings now expose semantic jamb width handles in uncropped conventional plans, with regenerated door arcs and host cuts, actual W/H readouts, source-revision fencing, sibling/assembly/join admission and one-command history. Release hosted_opening_resize and hosted_opening_resize_desktop cover both jambs, rotated hosts, stale and invalid proposals, undo/redo, save/reopen and output exclusion. Circular hosts now expose arc-station jamb controls with continuous pointer projection and Arc W readouts. Plan windows and native frame/sash/glass follow concentric arcs; curved doors use fitted chord leaves with explicit frame-head admission. Signed-normal material layers and nonoverlapping door glazing are corrected. Cropped/custom-frame handle workflows remain unavailable; property editing is retained. Native DXF/IFC assembly export and complete export acceptance remain open. Deterministic Debug/Release workflow evidence is hash-bound to the named sources and fixtures; the qualification boundary remains explicit.

manual_scenarios.steps: Enter a new edge length with **Move connected boundary chain** off and inspect the proposed outline and moved-point list. Apply each choice separately with Undo between them. Coincident geometry in a different object should remain unchanged unless it has an explicit supported relationship.

manual_scenarios.full_title: U064 — Insert a vertex into an edge
manual_scenarios.steps: Draw and close a rectangle, select it, choose **Insert boundary vertex**, and identify the edge by its number on the preview. Enter `0.5`; the green mark should appear halfway along that edge. Cancel once and confirm the drawing is unchanged, then reopen and Apply. Confirm the area total is unchanged. Drag the new corner to reshape the area and confirm the dimensions and total update. Undo the move and insertion, redo both, then save and reopen to check that the edited shape and dimensions remain. For a straight rectangle with no saved relationships, the coordinate freedom preview should show `8 → 10 (+2)`; with one saved horizontal relationship it should show `7 → 9 (+2)`.

manual_scenarios.steps: Open Colors on a customized component, change a color and Cancel. Reopen, check Use library colors and Apply. Undo and Redo.

Inspect the live proposal; cancel once, then repeat and commit. Undo and Redo.

manual_scenarios.steps: In a styled saved plan view, select a wall and open its length/constraint editor. Enter a new length and choose Preview. Cancel once, then repeat and Apply. Check the resulting wall, connected geometry and view-specific appearance. Undo the edit.

manual_scenarios.steps: In an Appraisal/Exterior project with an existing measured outline, draw and close a smaller wall loop inside it. Repeat with a loop crossing the original measured outline. Check the message, original measurement and physical walls; Undo and Redo.

manual_scenarios.full_title: U356 — Close a wall outline with a precise curved wall
manual_scenarios.steps: In an Appraisal/Exterior project, draw three sides of an outline. Press D for precise input. Choose a curved wall defined by its chord endpoint and angle, enter the original starting point as the endpoint and use a 90-degree sweep to close the outline. Inspect the exterior measurement, arc dimension and Details. Undo, Redo and save/reopen.

manual_scenarios.steps: Put two text labels and two components on different named layers. Export DXF and import the result into another project. Inspect source layers in the import review. Repeat with labels imported earlier into a chosen destination layer.

Press X; inspect the proposed horizontal side, then press Enter to accept it. Repeat with Y for a vertical side. Continue and close the outline. Repeat in Area mode and in Define First, placing each dimension before proposing the next side. Undo, Redo, save and reopen.

manual_scenarios.full_title: U366 — Align a drawing side with other walls using the arrow keys
manual_scenarios.steps: Draw a wall above the area where you will draw another outline. Start that outline below it. Press Ctrl+Right repeatedly to preview alignment with the existing wall's endpoint X coordinates, then Enter to accept the desired side. Try the other arrow directions. Press Ctrl+Shift+Arrow toward a wall crossing the cursor's horizontal or vertical path. Repeat in Area and Define First, placing each pending dimension before the next side. manual_scenarios.steps: In Area draw mode, create a closed outline with an internal divider and define its areas. Set one area's facts to dwelling and another to garage. Repeat with a curved wall.
